title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Practice: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
description: Practice using length × width × height to find rectangular prism volume.

questions.question: Which formula gives the volume of a rectangular prism?
questions.explanation: Rectangular prism volume uses all three dimensions: length, width, and height.

questions.question: A prism is 4 units long, 3 units wide, and 2 units high. What is its volume? Enter just the number.
Length × width finds one base layer of a rectangular prism.
questions.explanation: The base layer is a rectangle, so length × width counts cubes in one layer.

questions.question: A box is 8 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 5 cm high. What is its volume? Enter just the number.
Which unit is suitable for the volume of a prism with dimensions measured in meters?
questions.explanation: Volume uses cubic units, so meters become cubic meters.

questions.question: Explain why length × width alone is not enough for rectangular prism volume.
questions.correctAnswer: Length × width gives the area of one layer, but volume also needs height to count all the layers.
questions.explanation: Volume is 3D, so it requires length, width, and height.

questions.question: One layer has 18 cubes and there are 5 layers. What is the volume? Enter just the number.
A prism is 6 m long, 4 m wide, and 3 m high. Find the volume with units.
